headline: California Takes Action to Protect Young Social Media Users
meta_description: Governor Newsom signed laws limiting infinite scroll and autoplay for under-16 users, while requiring AI chatbots to include parental controls and safety featu…
summary_short: California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed landmark legislation designed to protect minors from addictive social media features and ensure AI chatbots include safeguard…
body:
California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed laws banning infinite scroll and autoplay on social media platforms for users under 16. The measures represent a significant step toward protecting young people from design features engineered to maximize engagement and screen time.

Beyond social media restrictions, the legislation also requires AI chatbots to implement parental controls and crisis protections. These safeguards aim to prevent minors from accessing harmful content and ensure they have access to support resources when needed.

The laws address growing concerns about how technology companies deliberately use addictive design patterns to keep younger users engaged. By targeting specific features like infinite scroll—which automatically loads new content without user action—and autoplay, California is attempting to interrupt the psychological mechanisms that make these platforms particularly compelling to developing brains.
quick_facts: California Governor Gavin Newsom signed the legislation
Bans infinite scroll and autoplay for users under 16
Requires AI chatbots to add parental controls
Includes crisis protections and safety features for minors
